paragraphs.text: Percentages in the adverse event summary table are reported with 0 decimals, and a count of zero is displayed without a percentage.
The planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) determines planned treatment: SFX50 is decoded as Low Dose, SFX100 as Medium Dose, SFX200 as High Dose, and PBO as Placebo.
Treatment emergence ends 14 days after the treatment end date, and that day is included in the window.
The planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) determines planned treatment: KRD5 is decoded as Low Dose, KRD10 as High Dose, and PBO as Placebo.
Percentages in the adverse event summary table are reported with 1 decimal, and a count of zero is displayed without a percentage.
The randomized set consists of every randomized subject.
The adverse event summary table has the rows ANY, RELATED, FATAL, in that order.
The adverse event summary table has the rows ANY, RELATED, FATAL, FATAL_RELATED, in that order.
The adverse event summary table has these rows: any event, related events, serious events, serious related events, fatal events, and events leading to discontinuation of study treatment.
The planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) determines planned treatment: TNB50 is decoded as Low Dose, TNB100 as Medium Dose, TNB200 as High Dose, and PBO as Placebo.
An adverse event is treatment-emergent if it starts on or after the first dose; date and time are compared where both were collected, and dates alone are compared otherwise.
An adverse event is considered related to study treatment when its causality is UNLIKELY RELATED, POSSIBLY RELATED, PROBABLY RELATED, or RELATED.
Actual treatment is the treatment named on the first exposure record of the subject (EX.EXTRT).
An adverse event is considered related to study treatment when its causality is POSSIBLY RELATED, PROBABLY RELATED, or RELATED.
Baseline body mass index is derived from baseline weight and height and is kept at full precision.
The planned arm code (DM.ARMCD) determines planned treatment: PBO is decoded as Placebo, ZQR200 as High Dose, ZQR100 as Medium Dose, and ZQR50 as Low Dose.
Percentages in the adverse event summary table are reported with 2 decimals, and a count of zero is displayed without a percentage.
The treatment end date is the latest start date among the exposure records that have a dose.
Age is grouped as below 65 years and 65 years and above.
